title: Financing a new business
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T08:14:01Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No bank point covers both internal and external sources of finance: the internal-finance point covers only internal sources, and the equity-and-debt point frames start-up money differently and omits investors and retained profits, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Financing a new business
card: A new business needs money and other resources before it can trade. It may need equipment, stock, a vehicle or a shop to rent.
money and resources that come from the owner, such as savings or a car the owner already has.
money that comes from outside the business, such as a loan from a bank or money from an investor.
Outside lenders and investors expect something in return. A lender may charge interest, and an investor may want a share of the profit.
draft.remember: Internal finance comes from the owner. External finance comes from others.

a.q: Priya starts a bakery in Bendigo. She pays for the oven with her own savings. What is this?
a.why: The money comes from the owner, so it is internal finance. It is not a loan or investor money, because those come from people outside the business.

b.q: Tom starts a bike repair shop in Geelong. He puts in $10,000 of savings and borrows $15,000 from a bank for tools. Which statement is correct?
opts: The savings are internal and the bank loan is external
The savings and the bank loan are both internal
The savings are external and the bank loan is internal
The savings and the bank loan are both external
b.why: Tom's savings come from the owner, so they are internal finance. The bank is outside the business, so its loan is external finance. Putting both together does not make the loan internal.
b.clue: Sort each amount by who provides it.

b.best: The savings are internal and the bank loan is external
